description: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02R4 is the fourth revision of the agency's bulletin on jamming and spoofing of global navigation satellite systems, issued on 3 July 2026 and corrected on 22 July 2026. It states that since February 2022 interference has grown in severity, intensity and sophistication, especially around conflict and geopolitical risk zones such as the south and eastern Mediterranean, Black Sea, Middle East, Baltic Sea and Arctic. It describes effects seen by crews, including spurious terrain alerts, corrupted ADS-B, inconsistent flight guidance and wrong time-dependent systems, and lists recommended actions. Producer: EASA (Cologne), drawing on the Network of Analysts and open sources; the list of affected flight information regions is kept on a separate EASA web page. Coverage: European airspace and neighbouring regions. Access: the bulletin is a free PDF attached to the Safety Publications Tool page. Licence and cost: free; the PDF carries the EASA copyright notice with all rights reserved. Caveats: it is qualitative guidance with no interference measurements, and recommendations are not mandatory. Simulation uses: it documents interference effects and operational responses for resilience and emergency-response scenarios of navigation-dependent aviation. Related records: the Tartu airport jamming case (case_study-tartu-airport-gnss-jamming-2024) and GPSJam (data-gpsjam-gnss-interference).
